newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jerusalem mayor says 3,500 homes planned for Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem mayor says 3,500 homes planned for Arabs.

text.p: Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert said on Monday 3,500 homes would be built in the city for Arabs while a Jewish neighbourhood is constructed on occupied Arab land.

Israel's plan to build some 6,500 homes for Jews on a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem has drawn international criticism and a warning from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat that it could disrupt the Middle East peace process.
Olmert said the plans for the Jewish and Arab houses would be approved on Wednesday and construction would start shortly after.

"We agreed a proposal will be presented that will enable the start of construction works in Har Homa and at the same time will enable the start of construction work in 10 neighbourhoods for Arabs," Olmert told Army Radio after a meeting with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"We are talking about some 3,500 housing units in 10 neighbourhoods and the detailed programme has already been presented to the prime minister and we went over its details."
Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem from Jordan in 1967 and annexed it. The final status of the city is an issue Israel and the Palestinians have agreed to discuss at peace talks.
The Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state while Israel wants to retain sovereignty of the whole city.

Arafat has called Israeli construction on the hill known to Arabs as Jabal Abu Ghneim and to Israelis as Har Homa "completely illegal" and warned it could arouse Palestinian rage that might end in bloodshed.
Olmert was asked about the building possibly leading to violence and said: "I hope very much there won't be negative implications."
